one_liner: A two-year research faculty post at NDU's think tank: publish peer-reviewed work on military drones and autonomous systems, brief generals, and teach.
fit_summary: This role requires a doctorate/ABD, or a master's plus five years of research focused specifically on unmanned and autonomous systems, along with a peer-reviewed publication record on the topic. Nothing on file shows Daniel has a graduate degree, publications, or autonomous-systems research, and the posting notes SCI clearance. Daniel's policy knowledge and people skills fit the engagement duties, but they do not meet the core requirements.
eligibility: Open to the public (Title 10 excepted service), so no federal status is needed; the appointment is not-to-exceed 2 years, with possible extension.

Education: you need a doctorate or ABD in a relevant field (public policy, political science, IR, etc.), or a master's plus at least five years in a research position focused on unmanned and autonomous systems.
You need a record of high-quality, peer-reviewed articles, books, or policy reports on unmanned and autonomous systems.
You need experience presenting research findings to DoW senior leaders, federal audiences, and industry executives.
The posting lists a Sensitive Compartmented Information clearance, and a current TS/SCI is desired, so expect to need SCI eligibility.
strategy: First, confirm honestly whether you hold a doctorate/ABD, or a master's with five years of autonomous-systems research; if not, skip this posting, because screeners apply the education rule strictly.
If you do qualify, list each publication on unmanned or autonomous systems with its full citation, and mark which ones are peer-reviewed.
Frame your IEM work only where it is true: research reports, tabletop exercises, or briefings for government clients. Do not stretch emergency management into defense autonomy.
Use the narrative assessment answers to give specific examples of briefing senior leaders and of policy impact, since the posting gives preference for demonstrated impact.
Keep the resume to two pages, with dates and hours per week, and apply before November 20, 2026.
A better use of your time is NDU or DoD policy, program analyst, or legislative roles that match your background, such as FEMA, Virginia VDEM, or county emergency management.
resume_bullets: Researched and authored [number] [report type] on [topic] for [government client] at IEM, using primary and secondary sources to support [decision/plan].
Designed and facilitated [number] tabletop exercises for [agency/audience size], presenting findings to [senior official level].
Briefed [audience] on [policy issue], resulting in [documented outcome, if any].
interview_questions: Describe your research agenda on unmanned and autonomous systems for the next two years and its implications for the defense industrial base.
Tell us about a time your research influenced defense strategy or policy.
How would you brief a General Officer on a complex technical finding in ten minutes?
What graduate-level course could you teach, and how would you structure it?
watch_outs: The degree and publication requirements appear unmet based on what is on file.
An SCI clearance is involved, and you have no clearance on record.
The appointment is temporary, not-to-exceed 2 years, and there is no administrative support staff, so you would handle your own paperwork.
